REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 9, 2020 -
07:00 P.M.
TELECONFERENCE MEETING AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20 VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 561 435 177
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, the City Council Chamber and City Hall are closed to the public. Consistent with State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the Los Angeles County Health Officer’s “Safer at Home Order for Control of COVID-19” the City Council will participate in the meeting through teleconference. Public participation in the meeting will be facilitated through the electronic methods as described below.
Agenda Materials:
The agenda and agenda packet related to items on this agenda are available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet will be made available for public inspection at www.cerritos.us.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION:
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us and on Cerritos TV3.
Public Comments:
Members of the public may provide public comment through the following methods:
Email: Members of the public may provide public comment by submitting an email to city_clerk@cerritos.us by 5:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the meeting date and agenda item number for which you would like to provide comment in the subject line of the email. The public comment will be distributed to all members of the City Council. During the meeting your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference participation: You may provide audio public comment by connecting to the teleconference meeting online or by telephone/mobile call (please select only one method). Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time on the agenda. You must be available to provide comment at the time your connection is “unmuted.” If you are not planning on providing public comment we encourage you to observe the meeting via livestream or on Cerritos TV3 to allow staff to more effectively manage the number of teleconference connections.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us04web.zoom.us/j/561435177
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: 1 (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 561 435 177
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) accommodations:
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer at 562-916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 561 435 177

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding emergency assistance to businesses available from
  the Small Business Administration.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor declared
  the public comments period closed.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

7D.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of March 12, 2020:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1032, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS TO ALIGN THE TERMS OF OFFICE FOR CERRITOS

  REPEALING SECTIONS 2.16.030, 2.18.030, 2.22.030 AND AMENDING TITLE 6

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City’s response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City & Theater Marketing Manager/City
  Librarian and Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Jim and Marcy McMahon requested additional assistance and information
  regarding the COVID-19 local emergency especially for seniors and those who are
  homebound. They submitted a document for the record. (The document is a
  public record and a full-text copy can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Tobi Balma expressed opposition to any closure of parks for passive recreation,
  including Heritage Park. She submitted a document for the record. (The document
  is a public record and a full-text copy can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Eddy N. expressed opposition to any closure of parks and requested the reopening
  of City parks by April 19, 2020. He submitted a document for the record. (The
  document is a public record and a full-text copy can be obtained in the Office of
  the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Murali Vasudevan thanked the Council for their work related to the COVID-19
  emergency and requested social media updates and daily emergency briefings.

  Mel Cortez thanked the Council for their work related to the COVID-19 emergency
  and suggested the Council work together regarding COVID-19 initiatives.

  Sam Desai spoke in support of providing more City-wide communication during the
  COVID-19 emergency.
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2020
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor declared
  the public comment period closed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract for fire alarm system replacement
  for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, Project No. 12716, Bid No. 1394-
  19 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comment period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Award a contract to JAM Corporation for the Fire Alarm System Replacement
  at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts in the amount of $1,088,000
  and reject the other bid; and
  2. Authorize the funds for the work to be drawn down from the Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts Endowment fund; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders. (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Edwards, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of an award of contract for annual financial auditing
  services (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given Ryan Carey, Finance Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Sam Desai expressed concerns with the request for proposals process as related
  to this item.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor declared
  the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to authorize the City
  Manager/Executive Director to execute the appropriate contract documents to
  facilitate the engagement of White, Nelson, Diehl, Evans as the City and Successor
  Agency auditors for a period of three (3) years, with two (2) additional years at the
  City’s option, inclusive of the following amendment in the contract documentation:

  Section II  NATURE OF SERVICES REQUIRED

  D. Irregularities and Illegal Acts
  Auditors shall be required to make an immediate, written report of all
  irregularities and illegal acts or indications of illegal acts of which they
  become aware to the following parties: City Council, City Manager, and
  City Attorney

  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Direct City staff to look into working in conjunction with the
  ABC Unified School District to plan a special event for High School seniors who are
  not able to experience their traditional graduation commencement programs due
  to the COVID-19 local emergency.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned in memory of Klete Ikemoto at 9:41 p.m.
